facts.statement: Polacanthus was an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs that lived in England during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 130 to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Polacanthus (from the Ancient Greek polys-/πολύς- "many" and akantha/ἄκανθα "thorn" or "prickle") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian dinosaurs from the early Cretaceous (130–125 million years ago) of England.

facts.statement: Polacanthus grew to a length of about 4 to 5 meters and its body was covered with armor plates and spikes.
facts.quote: It grew to about 4-5 m long. Its body was covered with armour plates and spikes.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Polacanthus is a basal member of the family Nodosauridae or belongs to a separate family called Polacanthidae.
facts.quote: It may be a basal member of the Nodosauridae or part of a separate family, the Polacanthidae.

facts.statement: The type species Polacanthus foxii was discovered by Reverend William Fox on the Isle of Wight in early 1865 at Barnes High on the southwest coast.
facts.quote: Polacanthus foxii was discovered by the Reverend William Fox on the Isle of Wight in early 1865, at Barnes High at the southwest coast.

facts.statement: In September 1865, Reverend William Fox reported the find in a lecture to the British Association and allowed Richard Owen to name the dinosaur Polacanthus foxii, possibly avoiding the convention against naming taxa after oneself.
facts.quote: In September 1865, Fox in a lecture to the British Association reported on the find and let it be named Polacanthus foxii by Owen, hereby perhaps circumventing the convention that an author does not name a taxon after himself.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen NHMUK PV R175 was found in the Upper Wessex Formation, which dates to the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, NHMUK PV R175, was found in a layer of the Upper Wessex Formation dating from the Barremian.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa described the specimen again in 1905 when it was mounted, providing the first illustration of the possible spike configuration.
facts.quote: In 1905, when it was mounted by the museum, the specimen was again described by Franz Nopcsa who for the first time provided an illustration of the possible spike configuration.

facts.statement: Darren Naish and David Martill estimated Polacanthus length at 5 meters in 2001, and Gregory S. Paul supported this length estimate in 2010 while suggesting a body mass of 2 tons.
facts.quote: In 2001, Darren Naish and David Martill estimated its length at 5 m. In 2010, Gregory S. Paul supported the initial length estimate, while providing a body mass estimate of 2 t.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz provided a lower size estimation for Polacanthus in 2012, suggesting a length of 4 meters and a mass between 227 and 454 kilograms.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz, in 2012, gave a lower estimation of 4 m and 227-454 kg.

facts.statement: Polacanthus had relatively long hindlimbs for an ankylosaur, with the holotype's right femur measuring approximately 55.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Its hindlimbs are relatively long for an ankylosaur, with the holotype right femur measuring about 55.5 cm in length.

facts.statement: A 2020 study identified a single unique trait for Polacanthus: the ischia curve toward each other at half their length, with their rear ends touching on the inner sides.
facts.quote: In 2020, a study concluded to a single autapomorphy: the ischia at half length curve towards each other, their rear ends touching at their inner sides.

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the pelvic shield measures 108 centimeters in width and 90 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: With the holotype, this shield is 108 centimetres wide and 90 centimetres long.

facts.statement: The smaller ossicles surrounding the larger osteoderms on the pelvic shield are sometimes completely fused to form flat armor plates.
facts.quote: These latter are sometimes completely fused to form flat armour plates.

facts.statement: In 1996, a species named Polacanthus rudgwickensis was described based on fragmentary fossils previously misidentified as Iguanodon.
facts.quote: In 1996, a Polacanthus rudgwickensis was named by Blows, after a review of some fossil material found in 1985 and thought to have been Iguanodon, which was on display at the Horsham Museum in Sussex.

facts.statement: Polacanthus lived during the Barremian age, approximately 124 to 132 million years ago.
facts.quote: Barremian age, approximately 124–132 million years ago.

facts.statement: In 2015, the species formerly known as Polacanthus rudgwickensis was reclassified into the separate genus Horshamosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2015, Blows made it a separate genus Horshamosaurus.

facts.statement: A 1971 attempt to rename Polacanthus foxii as Hylaeosaurus foxi was rejected and considered an invalid name.
facts.quote: In 1971, Polacanthus foxii was by Walter Coombs renamed into Hylaeosaurus foxi. This has found no acceptance, and the name is an invalid nomen ex dissertatione.

facts.statement: In 1928, Nopcsa described the genus Polacanthoides based on a scapula and limb bones previously referred to Hylaeosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1928, Nopcsa named a new genus and species Polacanthoides ponderosus, based on a number of syntypes: BMNH 2584, a left scapula found at Bolney which in 1841 by Gideon Mantell had been referred to Hylaeosaurus; and BMNH R1106 en 1107, a tibia and humerus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the genus Polacanthoides may be a chimera because its component bones likely belonged to Polacanthus.
facts.quote: This makes Polacanthoides a possible chimera, especially since their provenance from Wight makes it likely they belonged to Polacanthus.

facts.statement: In 1982, Justin Delair named the genus Vectensia based on a single armor plate found at Barnes High.
facts.quote: In 1982 Justin Delair named a genus Vectensia, without providing a specific name, based on specimen GH 981.45, an armour plate.

facts.statement: In 1987, Blows tentatively referred the genus Vectensia to the genus Polacanthus.
facts.quote: Blows in 1987 tentatively referred it to Polacanthus.

facts.statement: Fox assigned Polacanthus to Dinosauria in 1865, while Huxley and Hulke later assigned it to Scelidosauridae.
facts.quote: Fox in 1865 assigned Polacanthus to the Dinosauria, Huxley in 1870 and Hulke in 1881 assigned it to the Scelidosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1978, Coombs placed Polacanthus in the family Nodosauridae within the suborder Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: until Coombs in 1978 placed in the Nodosauridae within a larger Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: In 1996, Carpenter and colleagues refined the classification of Polacanthus to the subfamily Polacanthinae.
facts.quote: In 1996 Kenneth Carpenter e.a. refined this to the Polacanthinae.

facts.statement: Tracy Lee Ford proposed in 2000 that a distinct clade named Polacanthidae existed below the Nodosauridae and Ankylosauridae nodes.
facts.quote: An alternative hypothesis, first suggested by Tracy Lee Ford in 2000, is that there existed a clade Polacanthidae below the Nodosauridae + Ankylosauridae node.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Polacanthus is Polacanthus foxii.
facts.quote: name: Polacanthus foxii

facts.statement: Polacanthus foxii is the only known species of the extinct genus Polacanthus, a nodosaurid thyreophoran that lived in the Early Cretaceous, approximately 132 to 124 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Polacanthus foxii es la única especie conocida del género extinto Polacanthus (gr. "muchas púas") de dinosaurio tireóforo nodosáurido, que vivieron a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 132 y 124 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The type species Polacanthus foxii reached a length of between 4 and 5 meters.
facts.quote: Polacanthus foxii, la especie tipo, alcanzó entre 4 y 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Polacanthus was a quadrupedal dinosaur with avian hips and strong armor on its back.
facts.quote: Fue un dinosaurio con cadera de ave cuadrúpedo y con una fuerte armadura en su lomo.

facts.statement: Polacanthus was an ornithischian quadruped, also known as a bird-hipped dinosaur.
facts.quote: Polacanthus era un dinosaurio ornitisquio cuadrúpedo o "cadera de pájaro".

facts.statement: Polacanthus foxii was named after a fossil discovery on the Isle of Wight in 1865.
facts.quote: Polacanthus foxii recibió su nombre de un hallazgo en la Isla de Wight en 1865.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Polacanthus at 5 meters and its weight at 2 tons.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud en 5 metros y su peso en 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2012, Thomas Holtz provided a lower estimate of 4 meters in length and 227 to 454 kilograms in weight.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz dio una estimación más baja de 4 metros y 227-454 kilogramos en 2012.

facts.statement: Polacanthus had relatively long hind legs for an ankylosaur, with a right femur measuring 555 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: Sus patas traseras son relativamente largas para un anquilosaurio, con una longitud del fémur derecho de 555 milímetros.

facts.statement: In 2011, Barrett et al. identified two unique traits: a V-shaped groove on the neural canal floor and triangular-based, narrow-tipped tail spikes.
facts.quote: En 2011, Barrett et al indicó dos posibles rasgos únicos, las autapomorfias, el piso del canal neural está profundamente cortado por una ranura con un perfil transversal en forma de V y las espigas caudales tienen bases triangulares en vista lateral y puntas estrechas.

facts.statement: A 2020 study concluded that the unique trait of Polacanthus is its ischia curving toward each other at the mid-length, with their posterior ends touching internally.
facts.quote: En 2020, un estudio concluyó con una sola autapomorfia, los isquiones en la mitad de la longitud se curvan uno hacia el otro, sus extremos traseros se tocan en sus lados internos.

facts.statement: Hulke recognized that Polacanthus possessed a large pelvic or sacral shield, a single fused sheet of dermal bone over its hips decorated with tubercles.
facts.quote: Hulke entendió que Polacanthus tenía un gran "escudo pélvico" o "escudo sacro", una sola hoja fusionada de hueso dérmico sobre sus caderas, EL área sacra, que quizás no estaba adherida al hueso subyacente y decorada con tubérculos.

facts.statement: In the holotype, the pelvic shield measures 108 centimeters in width and 90 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: En el holotipo, este escudo mide 108 centímetros de ancho y 90 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The shield features four horizontal rows of keeled osteoderms on each side, surrounded by smaller bonelets.
facts.quote: Presenta cuatro filas horizontales de osteodermos con quillas más grandes por lado, rodeados por huesecillos más pequeños.

facts.statement: Hulke believed there were two rows of keeled osteoderms on each side of the tail.
facts.quote: Hulke pensó que en la cola había dos filas de osteodermos con quillas por lado.

facts.statement: Nopcsa hypothesized a different arrangement, suggesting two parallel rows of spikes on both the tail and the front of the body, including the neck.
facts.quote: Nopcsa planteó la hipótesis de un arreglo diferente. Pensó que tanto la cola como la parte delantera del cuerpo, incluido el cuello, presentaban dos filas paralelas de púas, una a cada lado.

facts.statement: In 2013, Henley Hobbs and his father discovered a footprint on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: En 2013, Henley Hobbs y su padre encontraron una huella en la Isla de Wight.

facts.statement: The type species Polacanthus foxii was discovered by Reverend William Fox on the Isle of Wight in 1865.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, P. foxii fue descubierta por el Reverendo William Fox en la Isla de Wight en 1865.

facts.statement: A second known specimen was found and excavated by Dr. William T. Blows in 1979.
facts.quote: El segundo espécimen conocido fue encontrado y excavado por el Dr William T. Blows en 1979

facts.statement: A second species, P. rudgwickensis, was named in 1996 by Dr. William T. Blows.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, P. rudgwickensis, fue nombrada en 1996 por el Dr. William T. Blows

facts.statement: Polacanthus foxii was discovered by Reverend William Fox on the Isle of Wight in early 1865 at Barnes High on the southwest coast.
facts.quote: Polacanthus foxii fue descubierto por el reverendo William Fox en la Isla de Wight a principios de 1865, en Barnes High en la costa suroeste.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from Greek polys meaning "many" and akantha meaning "spine", referring to the many spikes of the armor.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego πολύς, polys, "muchos" y ἄκανθα, akantha, "espina", en referencia a los muchos picos de la armadura.

facts.statement: The holotype BMNH R175 was found in a layer of the Upper Wessex Formation dating to the Barremian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, BMNH R175, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Wessex superior que data del Barremiense.

facts.statement: In 1905, Franz Nopcsa redescribed the specimen when it was mounted by the museum and provided the first illustration of the possible spike arrangement.
facts.quote: En 1905, cuando fue montado por el museo, el espécimen fue nuevamente descrito por Franz Nopcsa quien por primera vez proporcionó una ilustración de la posible configuración de picos.

facts.statement: In 1843, John Edward Lee reported the discovery on the Isle of Wight of three specimens consisting only of armor pieces.
facts.quote: En 1843, John Edward Lee informó del descubrimiento en Wight de tres de esos especímenes, que consistían solo en piezas de armadura.

facts.statement: A 2020 review of British ankylosaur fossils concluded that none of the additional specimens could be confidently referred to Polacanthus, leaving it represented only by the holotype.
facts.quote: Una revisión de 2020 de los fósiles de anquilosaurios británicos concluyó que ninguno de estos especímenes adicionales podría referirse con confianza a Polacanthus, que por lo tanto estaría representado solo por el holotipo.

facts.statement: The holotype is an incomplete skeleton lacking the head, neck, anterior armor, and hind limbs.
facts.quote: Es un esqueleto incompleto con la cabeza, el cuello, la armadura anterior y le falta de los miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: The holotype includes dorsal vertebrae, a sacral bar of five dorsosacral vertebrae, the sacrum, most of the pelvis, most of the left hind limb, the right femur, twenty-two tail vertebrae, ribs, chevrons, ossified tendons, a pelvic shield, twenty-two spikes, and numerous small bones.
facts.quote: Es un esqueleto incompleto al que le faltan la cabeza, el cuello, la armadura anterior y las extremidades anteriores, pero que incluye vértebras dorsales, una varilla sacra de cinco dorsosacrales, el sacro, la mayor parte de la pelvis, la mayor parte del miembro posterior izquierdo, el fémur derecho, veintidós cola. vértebras, costillas, cheurones, tendones osificados, un escudo pélvico, veintidós púas y numerosos huesecillos.

facts.statement: Hulke noted that the dermal armor had almost completely crumbled away due to significant deterioration over the years.
facts.quote: Hulke publicó la primera descripción detallada del hallazgo, señalando que el espécimen se había deteriorado mucho a lo largo de los años, y la armadura dérmica se había desmoronado casi por completo.

facts.statement: Many other specimens from the Isle of Wight and Great Britain have been referred to Polacanthus, mostly consisting of individual bones or armor elements.
facts.quote: Desde entonces, se han referido a Polacanthus muchos otros especímenes de Wight y Gran Bretaña. En su mayoría consisten en huesos individuales o elementos de armadura.

facts.statement: The genus Polacanthus is definitively known only from its type specimen, which represents the species P. foxii.
facts.quote: Polacanthus se conoce definitivamente solo por su espécimen holotipo, que representa la especie P. foxii.

facts.statement: In 1924, Edwin Hennig named Polacanthus becklesi after collector Samuel Beckles, based on a fragment of ilium associated with armor plates found on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: En 1924, Edwin Hennig nombró a un Polacanthus becklesi, el nombre específico en honor al coleccionista Samuel Beckles, basado en el espécimen BMNH R1926, un trozo de ilion asociado con placas de armadura, encontrado en Wight en el .

facts.statement: In 1996, William T. Blows named Polacanthus rudgwickensis based on fossil material found in 1985 that was previously thought to be Iguanodon and displayed at the Horsham Museum in Sussex.
facts.quote: En 1996, Polacanthus rudgwickensis fue nombrado por Blows, después de una revisión de algún material fósil encontrado en 1985 y que se cree que era Iguanodon, que estaba en exhibición en el Museo Horsham en Sussex.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen HORSM 1988.1546 is fragmentary and includes several incomplete vertebrae, a partial scapulocoracoid, the distal end of a humerus, an almost complete right tibia, rib fragments, and two osteoderms.
facts.quote: El material, holotipo HORSM 1988.1546, es fragmentario e incluye varias vértebras incompletas , un escapulocoracoideo parcial, el extremo distal de un húmero , una tibia derecha casi completa , fragmentos de costillas y dos osteodermos.

facts.statement: Named after the village of Rudgwick in West Sussex, this species was discovered in a quarry of the Rudgwick Brickworks Company within greenish-grey marl beds of the Wessex Formation, dating to the Barremian age approximately 124 to 132 million years ago.
facts.quote: Lleva el nombre de la aldea de Rudgwick en West Sussex y fue descubierto en una cantera de Rudgwick Brickworks Company, en el piso de la cantera en lechos de marga verde grisácea de la Formación Wessex, de edad barremiana, hace aproximadamente 124-132 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 2015, William T. Blows elevated Polacanthus rudgwickensis to a separate genus named Horshamosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2015, Blows lo convirtió en un género separado Horshamosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1928, Franz Nopcsa named the genus and species Polacanthoides ponderosus based on syntypes including a left scapula found in Bolney that Gideon Mantell had referred to Hylaeosaurus in 1841.
facts.quote: En 1928, Nopcsa nombró un nuevo género y especie Polacanthoides ponderosus, basándose en varios sintipos, BMNH 2584, una escápula izquierda encontrada en Bolney que en 1841 por Gideon Mantell había sido referida como Hylaeosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1982, Justin Delair named the genus Vectensia without a specific name, based on specimen GH 981.45, an armor plate.
facts.quote: En 1982, Justin Delair nombró un género Vectensia, sin proporcionar un nombre específico, basado en el espécimen GH 981.45, una placa de armadura.

facts.statement: Fox assigned Polacanthus to Dinosauria in 1865, while Huxley and Hulke assigned it to Scelidosauridae in 1870 and 1881 respectively.
facts.quote: Fox en 1865 asignó Polacanthus a Dinosauria, Huxley en 1870 y Hulke en 1881 lo asignó a Scelidosauridae.

facts.statement: In 1978, Walter Coombs placed Polacanthus in Nodosauridae within a larger Ankylosauria group.
facts.quote: Coombs en 1978 colocó en Nodosauridae dentro de una Ankylosauria más grande.

facts.statement: In 1996, Kenneth Carpenter and colleagues refined the classification to the subfamily Polacanthinae.
facts.quote: En 1996 Kenneth Carpenter et al. refinó esto a Polacanthinae.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis first suggested by Tracy Lee Ford in 2000 proposes the existence of a family-level clade called Polacanthidae below the node uniting Nodosauridae and Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Una hipótesis alternativa, sugerida por primera vez por Tracy Lee Ford en 2000, es que existiría un clado con nivel de familia llamado Polacanthidae debajo del nodo Nodosauridae más Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Polacanthus is Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Polacanthus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Polacanthus lived from the Berriasian to the Albian stages, approximately 139.1 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Albian (139.1 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Polacanthus rudgwickensis appears to have been approximately 30% longer than the type species P. foxii and differs from it in numerous vertebral and dermal armor characters.
facts.quote: P. rudgwickensis parece haber sido aproximadamente un 30% más largo que la especie tipo P. foxii y se diferencia de él en numerosos caracteres de las vértebras y la armadura dérmica .

facts.statement: Although the identification of Hoplitosaurus americanus as Polacanthus marshi gained some popularity in the early 1990s, this identity is generally rejected today.
facts.quote: Aunque esto ganó cierta popularidad a principios de la década de 1990, hoy en día la identidad es generalmente rechazada.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that Polacanthus is identical to Hylaeosaurus armatus, but this was rejected by Blows in 1987 due to differences in age and anatomy.
facts.quote: También se ha sugerido que Polacanthus sería simplemente idéntico a Hylaeosaurus armatus. Esto fue rechazado por Blows en 1987, debido a diferencias de edad y anatomía.

facts.statement: Determining a possible identity between Polacanthus and Hylaeosaurus is difficult to prove or refute because there are few overlapping elements in their holotypes.
facts.quote: Una posible identidad es difícil de probar o refutar ya que hay pocos elementos superpuestos en sus holotipos.
